'''Akar Kesh,''' or the '''Temple of Balance''', was one of nine temples of the [[Je'daii Order]] on the verdant world of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. Erected atop a towering pillar-like rock formation, the temple at Akar Kesh served as the Order's academy for instilling the ideals of balance in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] among its students.

==History==
[[File:AkarKesh-DotJ0.png|thumb|right|200px|Akar Kesh stood atop a giant rock pillar beneath the largest Tho Yor.]]
When the philosophers and scholars from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] first arrived on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]], they were brought forth from the stars on giant pyramidal constructs called the [[Tho Yor]]. These nine massive ships scattered across the planet and landed in separate locations, releasing those held within to settle the planet. The Tho Yor themselves would serve as the foundations for these travelers' new homes and places of study.<ref name="DOTJ0" />

The ninth and largest of these Tho Yor remained at the place where the others met, hovering above an open-air temple used by the [[Je'daii Order]] to teach balance through introspection and [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]]. A flat pavilion defined by eight thick minarets were all that made up the temple; at the center was a circular pool of water around which lessons were taught and [[Je'daii Master]]s waxed philosophically about the balance between Ashla and Bogan: the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="DOTJ0" /> The [[Je'daii Temple Master]], the Je'daii who served as steward of the facility and oversaw its functions, was often considered the wisest of all the Masters. In [[25,793 BBY]] Master [[Ketu]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]], was the Temple's overseer.<ref name="DOTJ0" />

==Behind the scenes==
The pinnacle and the foliage surrounding the temple depicted in ''Dawn of the Jedi 0'' is similar to what is found in [[Wikipedia: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park|Zhangjiajie National Forest Park]], which is famous for its pillar-like rock formations.
